readings.subsection: The Generations of Ishmael and Isaac
readings.title: The Death of Abraham
readings.subtitle: The Sons of Keturah and the Burial at Machpelah
readings.text: [Genesis 25:1] And Aḇraham took another wife, whose name was Qeturah. [2] And she bore him Zimran, and Yoqshan, and Meḏan, and Miḏyan, and Yishbaq, and Shuvaḥ. [3] And Yoqshan brought forth Sheḇa and Deḏan. And the sons of Deḏan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Le’ummim. [4] And the sons of Miḏyan were Ěphah, and Ěpher, and Ḥanoḵ, and Aḇiḏa, and Elda‛ah. All these were the children of Qeturah. [5] Now Aḇraham gave all <dn>את</dn> that he had to Yitsḥaq, [6] but to the sons of the concubines whom Aḇraham had, Aḇraham gave gifts while he was still living, and sent them away from his son Yitsḥaq, eastward, to the land of the east. [7] And these are all the years of Aḇraham’s life which he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years. [8] And Aḇraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, aged and satisfied, and was gathered to his people. [9] And his sons Yitsḥaq and Yishma‛ěl buried him in the cave of Maḵpělah, which is before Mamrě, in the field of Ephron son of Tsoḥar the Ḥittite, [10] the field which Aḇraham purchased from the sons of Ḥěth. There Aḇraham was buried with Sarah his wife. [11] And it came to be, after the death of Aḇraham, that <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed his <dn>את</dn> son Yitsḥaq. And Yitsḥaq dwelt at Be’ěr Laḥai Ro’i. [12] And this is the genealogy of Yishma‛ěl, Aḇraham’s son, whom Haḡar the Mitsrian, Sarah’s female servant, bore to Aḇraham. [13] And these were the names of the sons of Yishma‛ěl, by their names, according to their generations: The first-born of Yishma‛ěl, Neḇayoth; then Qěḏar, and Aḏbe’ěl, and Miḇsam, [14] and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, [15] Ḥaḏar, and Těma, Yetur, Naphish, and Qěḏemah. [16] These were the sons of Yishma‛ěl and these were their names, by their towns and their settlements, twelve chiefs according to their tribes. [17] And these were the years of the life of Yishma‛ěl: one hundred and thirty-seven years. And he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people. [18] And they dwelt from Ḥavilah as far as Shur, which is east of Mitsrayim as you go toward Ashshur. He settled before all his brothers.

readings.subsection: The Generations of Ishmael and Isaac
readings.title: The Birth of Esau and Jacob
readings.subtitle: The Sale of the Birthright
readings.text: [Genesis 25:19] And this is the genealogy of Yitsḥaq, Aḇraham’s son. Aḇraham brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq. [20] And Yitsḥaq was forty years old when he took <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah as wife, the daughter of Bethu’ěl the Aramean of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laḇan the Aramean. [21] And Yitsḥaq prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his wife, because she was barren. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered his prayer, and Riḇqah his wife conceived. [22] And within her the children struggled together, and she said, “If all is right, why am I this way?” So she went to ask <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>“Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your body. And one people shall be stronger than the other, and the older serve the younger.”</dq> [24] And when the days were filled for her to give birth, and see, twins were in her womb! [25] And the first came out red all over, like a hairy garment, so they called his name Ěsav. [26] And afterward his brother came out, with his hand holding on to Ěsav’s heel, so his name was called Ya‛aqoḇ. And Yitsḥaq was sixty years old when she bore them. [27] And the boys grew up. And Ěsav became a man knowing how to hunt, a man of the field, while Ya‛aqoḇ was a complete man, dwelling in tents. [28] And Yitsḥaq loved <dn>את</dn> Ěsav because he ate of his wild game, but Riḇqah loved <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ. [29] And Ya‛aqoḇ cooked a stew, and Ěsav came in from the field, and he was weary. [30] And Ěsav said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “Please feed me with that same red stew, for I am weary.” That is why his name was called Eḏom. [31] But Ya‛aqoḇ said, “Sell me your <dn>את</dn> birthright today.” [32] And Ěsav said, “Look, I am going to die, so why should I have birthright?” [33] Then Ya‛aqoḇ said, “Swear to me today.” And he swore to him, and sold his <dn>את</dn> birthright to Ya‛aqoḇ. [34] Ya‛aqoḇ then gave Ěsav bread and stew of lentils. And he ate and drank, and rose up and left. Thus Ěsav despised his <dn>את</dn> birthright.

readings.title: The Promise Renewed in Gerar
readings.subtitle: Isaac and Abimelech
readings.text: [Genesis 26:1] And there was a scarcity of food in the land, besides the first scarcity of food which was in the days of Aḇraham. And Yitsḥaq went to Aḇimeleḵ, sovereign of the Philistines, in Gerar. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him and said, <dq>“Do not go down to Mitsrayim, live in the land which <dn>I</dn> command you.</dq> [3] <dq>“Sojourn in this land. And <dn>I</dn> shall be with you and bless you, for <dn>I</dn> give all <dn>את</dn> these lands to you and your seed. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish the <dn>את</dn> oath which <dn>I</dn> swore to Aḇraham your father.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall increase your seed like the stars of the heavens, and <dn>I</dn> shall give all <dn>את</dn> these lands to your seed. And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,</dq> [5] <dq>“because Aḇraham obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice and guarded <dn>My</dn> Charge: <dn>My</dn> commands, <dn>My</dn> laws, and <dn>My</dn> Torot.”</dq> [6] And Yitsḥaq dwelt in Gerar. [7] And when the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” thinking, “lest the men of the place should kill me for Riḇqah, because she is good-looking.” [8] And it came to be, when he had been there a long time, that Aḇimeleḵ sovereign of the Philistines looked through a window, and he watched and saw Yitsḥaq playing with <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah his wife. [9] So Aḇimeleḵ called Yitsḥaq and said, “See, truly she is your wife! So how could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” And Yitsḥaq said to him, “Because I said, ‘Lest I die on account of her.’ ” [10] And Aḇimeleḵ said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people had almost lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us.” [11] And Aḇimeleḵ commanded all his people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife shall certainly be put to death.”

readings.title: The Contested Wells
readings.subtitle: Isaac's Prosperity and the Philistines' Envy
readings.text: [Genesis 26:12] And Yitsḥaq sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year a hundredfold, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed him. [13] And the man grew great and went forward until he became very great. [14] And he came to have possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and a great body of servants, and the Philistines envied him. [15] And the Philistines had stopped up all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Aḇraham his father, and filled them with dirt. [16] And Aḇimeleḵ said to Yitsḥaq, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.” [17] So Yitsḥaq went from there and pitched his tent in the wadi Gerar, and dwelt there. [18] And Yitsḥaq dug again the <dn>את</dn> wells of water which they had dug in the days of Aḇraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Aḇraham. And he called them by the names which his father had called them. [19] But when Yitsḥaq’s servants dug in the wadi and found a well of running water there, [20] the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Yitsḥaq’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” And he called the name of the well Ěseq, because they strove with him. [21] And they dug another well, and they strove over that one too, and he called its <dn>את</dn> name Sitnah. [22] And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not strive over it. And he called its <dn>את</dn> name Reḥoḇoth, and said, “For now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.” [23] And from there he went up to Be’ěrsheḇa. [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him the same night and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father Aḇraham. Do not fear, for <dn>I</dn> am with you, and shall bless you and increase your seed for <dn>My</dn> servant Aḇraham’s sake.”</dq> [25] And he built a slaughter-place there, and called on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he pitched his tent there, and the servants of Yitsḥaq dug a well there.

readings.title: The Treaty with Abimelech
readings.subtitle: Peace at Beersheba
readings.text: [Genesis 26:26] And Aḇimeleḵ came to him from Gerar, with Aḥuzzath, one of his friends, and Piḵol the commander of his army. [27] And Yitsḥaq said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing you have hated me and have sent me away from you?” [28] But they said, “We have clearly seen that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you. And we said, ‘Please, let there be an oath between us, between you and us. And let us make a covenant with you, [29] that you do no evil to us, as we have not touched you, and as we have done only good toward you, and have sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ” [30] And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank. [31] And they rose early in the morning and swore an oath with one another. And Yitsḥaq let them go, and they departed from him in peace. [32] And on the same day it came to be that the servants of Yitsḥaq came and informed him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.” [33] So he called it Shiḇah. Therefore the name of the city is Be’ěrsheḇa to this day. [34] And when Ěsav was forty years old, he took as wives <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏith the daughter of Be’ěri the Ḥittite, and <dn>את</dn> Basemath the daughter of Ělon the Ḥittite. [35] And they were a bitterness of spirit to Yitsḥaq and Riḇqah.

readings.title: Jacob Sent to Paddan Aram
readings.subtitle: Esau Marries Ishmael's Daughter
readings.text: [Genesis 28:1] And Yitsḥaq called Ya‛aqoḇ and blessed him, and commanded him, and said to him, “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kena‛an. [2] “Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethu’ěl your mother’s father. And take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laḇan your mother’s brother. [3] “And <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai bless you, and make you fruitful and increase you, and you shall become an assembly of peoples, [4] and give you the <dn>את</dn> blessing of Aḇraham, to you and your seed with you, so that you inherit the <dn>את</dn> land of your sojournings, which <dn>Elohim</dn> gave to Aḇraham.” [5] So Yitsḥaq sent <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ away, and he went to Paddan Aram, to Laḇan son of Bethu’ěl the Aramean, the brother of Riḇqah, the mother of Ya‛aqoḇ and Ěsav. [6] And Ěsav saw that Yitsḥaq had blessed <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ and sent him away to Paddan Aram to take himself a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kena‛an,” [7] and that Ya‛aqoḇ had obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan Aram. [8] So Ěsav saw that the daughters of Kena‛an did not please his father Yitsḥaq, [9] and Ěsav went to Yishma‛ěl and took <dn>את</dn> Maḥalath the daughter of Yishma‛ěl, Aḇraham’s son, the sister of Neḇayoth, to be his wife, besides the wives he had.

readings.title: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
readings.subtitle: The Vow of Jacob
readings.text: [Genesis 28:10] And Ya‛aqoḇ went out from Be’ěrsheḇa and went toward Ḥaran. [11] And he came upon a place and stopped over for the night, for the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it at his head, and he lay down in that place to sleep. [12] And he dreamed and saw a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens, and saw messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> going up and coming down on it. [13] And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood above it and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham your father and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq. The land on which you are lying, <dn>I</dn> give it to you and your seed.</dq> [14] <dq>“And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall break forth to the west and to the east, to the north and the south. And all the clans of the earth shall be blessed in you and in your seed.</dq> [15] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> am with you and shall guard you wherever you go, and shall bring you back to this land. For <dn>I</dn> am not going to leave you until <dn>I</dn> have done what <dn>את</dn> <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you.”</dq> [16] And Ya‛aqoḇ awoke from his sleep and said, “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in this place, and I did not know it.” [17] And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and this is the gate of the heavens!” [18] And Ya‛aqoḇ rose early in the morning, and took the <dn>את</dn> stone that he had put at his head, set it up as a standing column, and poured oil on top of it. [19] And he called the <dn>את</dn> name of that place Běyth Ěl, however, the name of that city had been Luz previously. [20] And Ya‛aqoḇ made a vow, saying, “Seeing <dn>Elohim</dn> is with me, and has kept me in this way that I am going, and has given me bread to eat and a garment to put on – [21] when I have returned to my father’s house in peace, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has been my <dn>Elohim</dn>, [22] then this stone which I have set as a standing column shall be <dn>Elohim</dn>’s house, and of all that <dn>You</dn> give me, I shall certainly give a tenth to <dn>You</dn>.”

readings.title: Isaac's Request of Esau
readings.subtitle: Rebekah's Deception
readings.text: [Genesis 27:1] And it came to be, when Yitsḥaq was old and his eyes were too dim to see, that he called <dn>את</dn> Ěsav his elder son and said to him, “My son.” And he answered him, “Here I am.” [2] And he said, “See now, I am old, I do not know the day of my death. [3] “Now then, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt wild game for me. [4] “And make me a tasty dish, such as I love, and bring it to me to eat, in order that my being does bless you before I die.” [5] And Riḇqah heard when Yitsḥaq spoke to Ěsav his son. And Ěsav went to the field to hunt wild game and to bring it. [6] And Riḇqah spoke to Ya‛aqoḇ her son, saying, “See, I heard your father speak to Ěsav your brother, saying, [7] Bring me wild game and make me a tasty dish to eat, and bless you in the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before my death.’ [8] “And now my son, listen to my voice according to what I command you. [9] “Please go to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, and I make a tasty dish from them for your father, such as he loves. [10] “And you shall take it to your father, and he shall eat it, so that he might bless you before his death.” [11] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to Riḇqah his mother, “See, Ěsav my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth-skinned man. [12] “What if my father touches me? Then I shall be like a deceiver in his eyes, and shall bring a curse on myself and not a blessing.” [13] But his mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go, get them for me.” [14] And he went and fetched them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made a tasty dish, such as his father loved. [15] And Riḇqah took the <dn>את</dn> best garments of her elder son Ěsav, which were with her in the house, and put them on <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ her younger son. [16] And she put the <dn>את</dn> skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck. [17] Then she gave the <dn>את</dn> tasty dish and the <dn>את</dn> bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Ya‛aqoḇ.

readings.title: Jacob Receives the Blessing
readings.subtitle: The Deception of Isaac
readings.text: [Genesis 27:18] And he went to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?” [19] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his father, “I am Ěsav your first-born, I have done as you said to me. Please rise, sit and eat of my wild game, so that your being might bless me.” [20] But Yitsḥaq said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brought it to me.” [21] Then Yitsḥaq said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “Please come near, so that I feel you, my son, whether you truly are my son Ěsav or not.” [22] And Ya‛aqoḇ went near to Yitsḥaq his father, and he felt him and said, “The voice is the voice of Ya‛aqoḇ, but the hands are the hands of Ěsav.” [23] And he did not recognise him, for his hands were hairy like his brother Ěsav’s hands, and he blessed him. [24] And he said, “Are you truly my son Ěsav?” And he said, “I am.” [25] And he said, “Bring it near to me, and let me eat of my son’s wild game, so that my being might bless you.” So he brought it near to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank. [26] And his father Yitsḥaq said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.” [27] And he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him and said, “See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed. [28] And <dn>Elohim</dn> give you of the dew of the heavens, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and wine. [29] Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be those cursing you, and blessed be those blessing you!”

readings.title: Esau's Lost Blessing
readings.subtitle: Jacob Flees to Haran
readings.text: [Genesis 27:30] And it came to be, as soon as Yitsḥaq had finished blessing <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ, and Ya‛aqoḇ had hardly left the presence of Yitsḥaq his father, that Ěsav his brother came in from his hunting. [31] And he too had made a tasty dish and brought it to his father, and said to his father, “Let my father rise and eat of his son’s wild game, so that your being might bless me.” [32] And his father Yitsḥaq said to him, “Who are you?” And he said, “I am your son, your first-born, Ěsav.” [33] Then Yitsḥaq trembled exceedingly, and said, “Who was it then who hunted wild game and brought it to me? And I ate all of it before you came, and I have blessed him. Yes, he is blessed.” [34] When Ěsav heard the <dn>את</dn> words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, me too, O my father!” [35] And he said, “Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing.” [36] And Ěsav said, “Was his name, then, called Ya‛aqoḇ? For he has caught me by the heel these two times. He took my <dn>את</dn> birthright, and see, now he has taken my blessing!” And he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?” [37] Then Yitsḥaq answered and said to Ěsav, “See, I have made him your master, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants. And I have sustained him with grain and wine. And what, then, shall I do for you, my son?” [38] And Ěsav said to his father, “Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me too, O my father!” And Ěsav lifted up his voice and wept. [39] And Yitsḥaq his father answered and said to him, “See, your dwelling is of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the heavens from above. [40] And by your sword you are to live, and serve your brother. And it shall be, when you grow restless, that you shall break his yoke from your neck.” [41] And Ěsav hated Ya‛aqoḇ because of the blessing with which his father blessed him, and Ěsav said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father draw near, then I am going to kill <dn>את</dn> my brother Ya‛aqoḇ.” [42] And the <dn>את</dn> words of Ěsav her older son were reported to Riḇqah, and she sent and called Ya‛aqoḇ her younger son, and said to him, “See, your brother Ěsav comforts himself concerning you, to kill you. [43] “And now, my son, listen to my voice, and rise, flee to my brother Laḇan in Ḥaran. [44] “And stay with him a few days, until your brother’s wrath turns away, [45] until your brother’s displeasure turns away from you, and he forgets what <dn>את</dn> you have done to him. And I shall send and bring you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?” [46] And Riḇqah said to Yitsḥaq, “I am disgusted with my life because of the daughters of Ḥěth. If Ya‛aqoḇ takes a wife from the daughters of Ḥěth, like these who are the daughters of the land, what is my life to me?”
